Adding technical context and proposed measurement details. Short answers up front: yes, we can run the like-for-like. We’ll instrument to capture p50/p95/p99, tail-buffer events, tokens/sec, KV hit rate, batch sizes, and CPU/GPU utilization.

Proposed harness:
- Inference harness: containerized runner that replays your prompt set with identical inter-request timing and sequence length distribution.
- Two variants:
  A) Default config (continuous batching target latency 80ms, dynamic kernel selection).
  B) Quantized profile + cache-forward (aggressive KV caching for repeated prefixes) + slightly higher batch window (to favor throughput).
- Metrics emitted: p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies (ms), tokens/sec, throughput (tokens/s), GPU utilization (%), memory headroom (GB), per-token cost estimate (USD/token).

Initial estimate (from small sample run):
- HyperCloud baseline (customer-run numbers): p95 210ms, p99 420ms, tokens/sec ~9.8k
- Redwood default (our lab run on similar hardware, same model): p95 190ms, p99 320ms, tokens/sec ~11.4k
- Redwood quantized variant (est): p95 170ms, p99 290ms, tokens/sec ~13.1k but with potential ~1.5% accuracy delta on golden prompts.

Notes/risks: quantization gains depend on model architecture and offload paths; we’ll flag any hallucination/regression cases. We recommend running the golden-prompt accuracy suite in parallel to ensure <=2% drift.

I’ll push a reproducible CSV and a short dashboard after the run.
